Adapted from c-testsuite [tests/single-exec/00156.c](https://github.com/c-testsuite/c-testsuite/blob/5c7275656d751de0e68b2d340a95b5681858ed07/tests/single-exec/00156.c), whose pinned [.otags](https://github.com/c-testsuite/c-testsuite/blob/5c7275656d751de0e68b2d340a95b5681858ed07/tests/single-exec/00156.c.otags) identify TinyCC `tests/tests2/04_for.c` at commit `61ba9f229955f105af9d7dcdbfcc9c9effbe8af3`. The upstream [README](https://github.com/mirror/tinycc/blob/61ba9f229955f105af9d7dcdbfcc9c9effbe8af3/README) specifies GNU LGPL and [COPYING](https://github.com/mirror/tinycc/blob/61ba9f229955f105af9d7dcdbfcc9c9effbe8af3/COPYING) supplies LGPL v2.1; the adapted code retains that license, with a copy at [LICENSE.tinycc](../LICENSE.tinycc), not c-testsuite's top-level MIT license. The original inclusive for loop in main is extracted into a bounded series_sum function, parameterizing its upper bound and accumulating the printed integers instead of doing I/O. The mutation changes the inclusive loop test from <= to <, dropping the final term. The main function and eight-input reference driver were added for this corpus; this is a source-derived reduction, not a claim to replay the complete original test.
